method: Ranked by claude-sonnet-5-5, which read 12 of 14 shortlisted pieces

picks.title: Seeing the machine code of your Java program, with a few lines of Java
picks.author: Daniel Lemire
picks.why_it_matters: Shows how to profile JIT output per instruction; a bitCount loop on ARM stalls on a false dependency through one vector register, fixed 7x by JDK 27 vectorization.

picks.title: How Public Evals Work, Where They Break, and What Should Change
picks.why_it_matters: Audits twelve public evals: graders fail correct work, all-pass scoring is brittle, and pass^k reliability reveals what average pass rate hides.

picks.title: Our Son Is Practicing in the Basement for His Interplanetary Voyage
picks.author: Peter Stamm
picks.why_it_matters: Peter Stamm's story of a son rehearsing a Mars voyage in the basement, with message delays counted in minutes, is a quiet study of distance and parental love.

picks.title: Is Norway’s Oil Fund a Blessing or a Curse?
picks.author: D. T. Max
picks.why_it_matters: The $2.3 trillion oil fund as a cultural problem: how a thrifty, egalitarian nation manages a windfall and a brash, finance-bro manager, with economic and strategic stakes.

picks.title: A colossal oscillation
picks.author: Dagomar Degroot
picks.why_it_matters: An environmental historian uses archives of society and nature to argue El Niño is hard to define and forecast, and that its human effects are partly made by people.
